finding.claim: The POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban handler wraps require_admin in a broad except Exception with no re-raise or return, so the 403 from abort(403) is swallowed and do_ban(uid) runs for non-admin callers, returning {"ok": true}. Severity HIGH; becomes CRITICAL if upstream middleware gives anonymous requests a dict g.user.
finding.source: Authenticated non-admin caller (any request where g.user is a dict with falsy is_admin) sending POST to /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid in the URL path (admin.py:14-15).
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 (protected account-ban operation; a stub in this repo).

trace.note: Route POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban registered; uid taken from the URL path.
require_admin(g.user) called; g.user is populated by upstream middleware not present in this repo.
require_admin checks user.get('is_admin'); falsy for a non-admin.
abort(403) raises werkzeug Forbidden, a subclass of Exception.
except Exception catches Forbidden; no raise or return, so execution falls through.
log.warning records the failed check and g.user.get('name'); if g.user is unset this raises AttributeError and do_ban is not reached.
jsonify(ok=True) returns HTTP 200 to the non-admin caller.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) is correct but its abort is caught by the caller, so it fails open. methods=['POST'] restricts only the verb; no CSRF token check is visible in this file. g.user unset causes AttributeError at line 19, which blocks the bypass only for requests without a user. No decorator, blueprint or before_request in this file enforces the admin role. The sibling unban handler (lines 24-28) calls require_admin without the wrapper and is not affected. Semgrep was not run (Bash disabled); upstream g.user middleware was not reviewed because it is not in the repository.

verdict.guard_found: none effective. require_admin (admin.py:9-11) does abort(403), but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19) with no re-raise or return, so the 403 is swallowed and do_ban(uid) runs at admin.py:20. The unban handler (admin.py:24-28) calls require_admin unwrapped and is not affected. No before_request or decorator in this repo enforces admin. Upstream g.user middleware is not in the repo; if g.user is unset, line 17 raises AttributeError, line 19 raises again, and do_ban is never reached, so the bypass needs g.user to be a dict.
verdict.reason: The trace matches admin.py:14-21 exactly: require_admin's abort(403) at admin.py:11 is caught by the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18 with no re-raise, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs and jsonify returns ok=True for any authenticated caller whose g.user is a dict with a falsy is_admin. The only residual uncertainty is the upstream auth middleware, which is not in this repo.
